scenes.line1: Why do APIs need different HTTP methods?
scenes.say: Why do APIs use different HTTP methods, and what makes HTTP version two such a big deal?

scenes.label: GET
scenes.say: Let's start with methods. Get fetches data. Post sends new data. Put updates, and Delete removes. Each tells the server your intent.
HTTP version one point one is text-based and handles one request at a time. HTTP two brings multiplexing and header compression. HTTP three runs over QUIC for even faster, more reliable connections.

scenes.question: What does HTTP/2 multiplexing mean?
scenes.wrong: It combines several responses into one.
scenes.right: It lets multiple requests share a single connection at once.
scenes.say: Watch out: multiplexing in HTTP two means multiple requests can share one connection, not that responses are merged together.
